title: Handoff-proxy coordination and liveness-graded switchover for VPC data-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a coordinated handoff and liveness-graded switchover mechanism for Private (VPC) data-plane/runtime upgrades. The goal is zero customer-visible downtime for sessions with active KV/prefix caches and long-lived TCP/HTTP connections by introducing a small, transparent handoff proxy layer, graded liveness gates, and Terraform/IaC module hooks to ensure safe rollout and predictable rollback. This ticket covers orchestration, health gating rules, prewarm/priming behavior, and the rollback playbook for stateful tenants.
background: Current private runtime upgrades rely on coarse drain-and-swap procedures. Customers with long lived sessions, primed KV caches, or strict latency SLOs occasionally observe transient errors or cold-start latency spikes during upgrades. Existing rollouts lack a coordinated handoff for in-flight connections and do not differentiate liveness (ready vs degraded) when shifting traffic, leading to noisy rollbacks and manual intervention.
goals: 1) Add a handoff proxy shim that sits in front of runtime nodes in VPC deployments and supports transparent connection draining and state handover. 2) Implement graded liveness gating (green/yellow/red) and use it to drive traffic shift policies in the orchestrator. 3) Extend Terraform modules and IaC hooks so upgrades deploy proxies, prewarm caches, and enforce health-gates automatically. 4) Provide a tested rollback playbook that can selectively revert only affected tenant slices without global downtime.
non_goals: 1) Replacing customer-managed ingress or VPN topology. 2) Implementing new network overlay tech or changing IP addressing models. 3) Full rewrite of the runtime — we will add a small proxy and orchestration hooks only.
acceptance_criteria: Handoff proxy is deployed by Terraform module into a customer VPC in a canary slice configuration
During a staged upgrade with synthetic and production traffic, 99.95% of requests for active sessions see no error and median p95 token latency change <= 10ms
Graded liveness metrics (green/yellow/red) are computed from readiness probe, KV priming status, and tail-latency SLO and exposed in Console per-tenant
Orchestrator automatically halts or rolls back traffic for a slice when liveness enters red for > 30s
Rollback playbook can revert a single slice with no disruption to other slices and records automated postmortem annotations
Terraform module includes optional flags: enable_handoff_proxy (bool), priming_workers (int), probe_window_seconds (int) and is documented
E2E test harness reproduces a simulated network partition and validates our connection handoff/transparent retry behavior
implementation_notes: High level: implement a small Go-based handoff proxy that terminates inbound connections and multiplexes to runtime pods. Proxy responsibilities: TLS passthrough / termination depending on config, sticky session mapping with transparent connection transfer where possible, graceful drain that signals runtime to snapshot active KV entries for priming, and exposes liveness endpoints used by the orchestrator. Orchestrator changes: implement graded liveness state machine (green/yellow/red) using aggregated probes, priming completeness, and latency signals. Terraform: add new module and variables; sequence: deploy proxy -> deploy new runtime nodes -> priming -> shift traffic via orchestrator. Prioritize minimal heap and CPU for proxy to keep cost low. Security: HSM/KMS keys must be accessible per existing Private deployment KMS pattern. Ensure TLS cert rotation works through proxy. Use feature flag for progressive rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for proxy connection handling, integration tests for handoff under synthetic load, chaos tests for network flaps, and canary e2e with a sandbox tenant in staging. Create a local-integration harness with an in-memory KV store to validate priming/restore. Write terraform plan/unit tests using Terratest to validate module idempotency. Add a canary job that runs a scripted session workload and verifies no broken sessions during rollouts. Include performance microbenchmarks to ensure proxy adds <5ms median overhead under normal load.
rollout_strategy: 1) Feature-flag rollout in staging: enable_handoff_proxy=false by default. 2) Deploy proxy to a small staging slice and run synthetic sessions. 3) Enable proxy on canary tenant group in staging and run full e2e. 4) In production, enable on 1% tenant-slices with strict observability. Orchestrator will progress using a graded-live policy: green->20% traffic shift over 60s, yellow->pause and run additional priming, red->rollback slice. Use automated priming jobs and synthetic traffic bursts during green/yellow windows. Monitor cost and latency for 2 hours at each stage before expanding to next percentage. Provide manual override in Console to cancel or accelerate.
rollback_playbook: Immediate: If slice enters red for >30s, orchestrator automatically re-routes traffic back to previous generation and marks slice as 'rollback-in-progress'. Run automated snapshot restore of KV cache from pre-upgrade snapshot. Notify SRE/solutions on-call via PagerDuty and create an incident ticket with slice id. If automatic rollback fails, follow manual steps: 1) run terraform apply to revert runtime ASG/pool to previous AMI/image, 2) redeploy handoff proxy with previous config, 3) run scripted reconnect utility to reconcile client sessions. Post-incident: capture timeline, root cause, and add learnings to the upgrade-runbook. All rollback operations must be reversible by IaC within 15 minutes.
telemetry_and_alerts: New telemetry: handoff_proxy_active_connections, proxy_drain_inflight_seconds, priming_completion_ratio, graded_liveness_state{green,yellow,red}, slice_rollback_count. Console dashboards: per-tenant liveness timeline, rollout progression view, and token-latency distribution during upgrades. Alerts: PagerDuty if more than 3 slices in red simultaneously, or p95 token latency regression >20% for >5 minutes. Add internal audit logs for every traffic-shift decision and automated rollback trigger.
dependencies: ENG-391204 (evacuate-first-hot-switchover-controller) - for integration with evacuation APIs
PM-842 - upgrade-runbook and customer communication templates
Security-201 - KMS access pattern review for proxy key usage
risks: 1) Proxy becomes a single point of failure if misconfigured — mitigate with autoscaling, health checks, and multi-AZ placement. 2) Additional latency or resource cost from proxy layer — mitigate via benchmarking and minimal resource footprint. 3) Complexity in priming/restore for very large KV caches — mitigate with partial warm strategies and incremental priming. 4) Customer network/topology differences may reveal edge cases — mitigate with staged customer pilot and careful terraform module opt-in.
outstanding_questions: 1) Should the proxy perform TLS termination by default or offer a passthrough-only mode? 2) What is the maximum safe priming window for tenants with >100GB KV caches? 3) Do we want to expose the graded-liveness API to customers for their own observability?
notes: Coordinate with Solutions and SRE to pick pilot customers. Schedule a dry-run upgrade for the staging cluster next sprint. Plan for a tabletop exercise with on-call rotation to validate rollback playbook.
